items.confirm: The Nifty holds above 24,000 after the open with foreign buying continuing.
items.kill: Profit-taking near 24,000 erases the gap and the index closes lower.

seeds.why: Cheaper oil and foreign buying lift the index heavyweight.
Foreign inflows favour the largest private bank.

items.summary: The Nifty 50 closed at 23,960.60 (+0.63%) and the Sensex at 77,301.40 (+0.50%) on Wednesday, a fifth straight gain, with small caps up about 2% and 36 of 50 Nifty stocks higher. Overnight the Dow jumped 3.03% and the S&P 500 1.58% as Brent fell 8.7%, and GIFT Nifty traded at 24,369.50 (+1.75%) at 2:41 am IST, pointing to a gap-up open.
items.title: Nifty gains for a fifth day to a two-month closing high of 23,961 as Democrats win Congress
items.whyItMatters: A gap above 24,000 would test whether the five-day foreign-buying rally can extend past resistance.

affects.how: raises the bar for AI demand

items.confirm: IT keeps lagging even as the broader market rises.
items.kill: A rebound as US megacap gains outweigh the data-centre worry.

seeds.why: US scrutiny of AI capex clouds deal flow.
Fell about 3% on the Texas data-centre moratorium pledge.

items.summary: TCS fell 2.52% to ₹2,436, HCLTech 2.37% and Infosys 1.73% on Wednesday as Nifty IT dropped 1.5%, the only sector down. Overnight Microsoft rose about 7% and Apple 5%, but Nvidia fell about 3% and Micron more than 7% after Texas's incoming governor pledged a moratorium on new data-centre approvals; Qualcomm fell about 7% after hours and Korea's Kospi opened about 2.7% lower on worries that Congress will scrutinise AI capex.
items.title: IT stocks fall 1.5% as investors weigh what a Democratic Congress means for AI spending
items.whyItMatters: US policy on AI spending is now moving Indian IT services stocks independently of the wider market.

affects.how: lower oil and a firmer rupee ease imported inflation

items.confirm: USD/INR opens below 94.5 and stays there.
items.kill: The RBI buys dollars to rebuild reserves and the pair rises.

nse.why: Fuel and dollar costs both fall.
Exporter in focus as the rupee firms.

seeds.why: A firmer rupee and cheaper fuel cut airline costs.
A firmer rupee trims exporters' rupee revenue.

items.summary: The rupee settled at a provisional 94.58 per dollar on Wednesday (HDFC Sky/PTI), up 17 paise, after trading 94.50–94.87; Reuters put the close at 94.64. Overnight the dollar index fell 0.34% to 101.53 and Brent fell 8.7%, while foreign investors bought a net ₹7,284 crore of Indian shares on Wednesday.
items.title: Rupee firms for a fourth day to 94.64 as the dollar slips after the US midterms
items.whyItMatters: Cheaper oil and foreign inflows ease pressure on India's import bill and the rupee.

items.confirm: Brent holds below $100 as talks continue.
items.kill: A new strike or failed talks sends Brent back above $100.
items.summary: The slide deepened: Brent for January settled at $94.62, down 8.7%, after touching $93.22, its lowest since 31 Aug, and WTI settled at $88.12 (−8.3%), its biggest drop since May (Bloomberg via Rigzone). Traders bet a Democratic Congress speeds an end to the Iran war; trend-following funds cut longs, and JPMorgan says the market is back in surplus. Iran called the US reply to its Hormuz plan 'unconvincing' and the IRGC claimed four tankers hit by mines, while Qatar-mediated talks continue.
items.title: Brent slips toward $102 as the Democratic sweep and Trump's 'no new strikes' remark trim the war premium
items.whyItMatters: Oil near $95 instead of $115 cuts India's import bill, inflation and costs for paints, airlines and oil marketers.

affects.how: sets up payrolls as the next test

items.confirm: Yields stay near 4.9% into payrolls.
items.kill: A jobless-claims surprise or hawkish Fed talk lifts yields sharply.

seeds.why: Lower US yields support foreign flows into Indian banks.

items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield closed about 6 bp lower near 4.89% on Wednesday (Yahoo Finance shows 4.894%) and the 2-year about 5 bp lower at 4.59%, as investors priced fiscal gridlock and oil fell. The Treasury kept its quarterly refunding at $125 billion, and December Fed-hike odds slipped to about 77% (CME FedWatch); weekly jobless claims come today and payrolls on Friday.
items.title: Treasury yields fall about 5 bp to 4.92% as Democrats sweep Congress
items.whyItMatters: Lower US yields ease pressure on emerging-market currencies and support foreign flows into India.

items.confirm: ARPU at or above ₹268 with margin expansion.
items.kill: ARPU misses or subscriber growth slows.
items.summary: Bharti Airtel closed at ₹2,067.60 (+0.13%) on Wednesday, pausing after a 3.8% pre-results run, and reports today. Kotak expects revenue of about ₹59,750 crore (+14.5%) and Axis Direct ₹60,061 crore (+15.2%), with profit estimates of ₹8,725–10,618 crore and ARPU of ₹268–269 (Business Standard).
items.title: Bharti Airtel reports September-quarter results; brokerages expect 14–15% revenue growth and ARPU near ₹268
items.whyItMatters: Airtel's ARPU is the first big read on Indian telecom pricing since Jio's listing.

items.confirm: Jewellery growth near 27% with steady margins.
items.kill: Margins slip on high gold prices or growth misses.
items.summary: Titan rose 4.22% to ₹4,754.40 on Wednesday, among the top Nifty gainers, and reports today; Kotak Neo's preview expects profit of ₹1,274–1,419 crore (about +27%) and jewellery growth of 27–28%. Gold settled about 3.4% higher at roughly $4,073 an ounce overnight, its biggest daily gain since August.
items.title: Titan jumps 4.2% ahead of Dhanteras and its September-quarter results on 5 Nov
items.whyItMatters: Titan's jewellery growth is the main listed read on festive gold demand.

items.confirm: Foreign buying continues and HDFC Bank holds its gains.
items.kill: Profit-taking after a 5% two-day run.

seeds.why: Foreign buying concentrates in the largest private bank.

items.summary: HDFC Bank rose 1.54% to ₹736.70 on Wednesday, taking its two-day gain to about 5%, as foreign investors bought a net ₹7,284 crore of Indian shares (5paisa) after ₹6,837 crore on Tuesday. Nifty Bank rose 0.67% to 55,913.60, and US 10-year yields fell about 6 bp overnight.
items.title: HDFC Bank extends its run as foreign buying lifts private lenders
items.whyItMatters: HDFC Bank is the biggest single channel for foreign money into Indian equities.

items.confirm: Results and dividend in line and the stock tracks the market.
items.kill: A sharp sell-off on oil or a dividend surprise.
items.summary: ONGC closed at ₹235.00 (+1.2%) on Wednesday before its board meeting today on results and an interim dividend. Overnight Brent settled 8.7% lower at $94.62, US energy was the worst S&P sector (−4.74%, ExxonMobil −5.3%), and PetroChina fell more than 5% in Hong Kong this morning.
items.title: ONGC's board meets on 5 Nov for results and an interim dividend as Brent slips toward $102
items.whyItMatters: ONGC's realisations move almost one for one with Brent, which has fallen more than 15% this week.

items.confirm: Brokerages lift estimates on volumes.
items.kill: Margin worries outweigh volumes.
items.summary: Dabur reported after Wednesday's close: profit up 11.7% to ₹505.5 crore and revenue up 11.6% to ₹3,563 crore, with India FMCG volume growth of 5.5% but operating margin down 60 bp; it declared an interim dividend of ₹3.50 (record date 10 Nov). The stock had already risen 3.45% to ₹394.10 before the numbers as Nifty FMCG rose 1.5%.
items.title: Dabur's profit rises 12% to ₹506 crore on 5.5% volume growth, but margins slip
items.whyItMatters: Dabur's volumes show whether rural and festive demand is holding up for FMCG.

items.confirm: US futures hold the gains and megacaps keep leading.
items.kill: A reversal as the data-centre worry spreads beyond chips.

nse.why: Indian AI-server maker exposed to the US chip mood.

seeds.why: Down about 3% on the data-centre moratorium pledge.

items.summary: The Dow closed at 53,356.12 (+1,569.40, +3.03%), the S&P 500 at 7,688.62 (+1.58%) and the Nasdaq at 25,736.51 (+1.44%) as investors priced fiscal gridlock and cheaper oil; the VIX fell 20% to 16.61. Microsoft rose about 7%, Amazon 6% and Apple 5% to a record, while Nvidia fell about 3%, Micron more than 7% and CoreWeave 10% after Texas's incoming governor pledged a data-centre moratorium; energy (−4.74%) and defence (Lockheed −7%) lagged.
items.title: Dow jumps 3% for its best day since April 2025 as Democrats win Congress; Big Tech rallies, chip stocks slide
items.whyItMatters: A risk-on US close with a split inside tech sets up a strong open for Asia and India but a cautious one for AI hardware.

affects.how: higher prices may slow festive volumes

items.confirm: Gold holds above $4,000.
items.kill: The dollar rebounds and gold gives back the gain.
items.summary: COMEX December gold settled about 3.4% higher at roughly $4,073 an ounce (Reuters via Bloomingbit), its largest one-day gain since 19 Aug, after the dollar index fell to about 101.5 on the Democratic sweep; spot silver traded near $52.32. Gold had touched a one-year low on 2 Nov.
items.title: Gold jumps 3.4% to about $4,073, its biggest gain since August, as the dollar slides
items.whyItMatters: A rebounding gold price lifts jewellers' inventory values and gold-loan collateral just before Dhanteras.

items.confirm: Qualcomm opens sharply lower and peers follow.
items.kill: Data-centre ambitions outweigh handset weakness.

nse.why: Indian phone assembler in focus on handset demand.

seeds.why: Shares fell about 7% after hours on guidance.
Apple's in-house modem ramp cuts Qualcomm's share.

items.summary: Qualcomm's fiscal Q4 EPS of $2.17 was in line and revenue of $10.44 billion beat $10.14 billion, but Q1 EPS guidance of $2.15–2.35 bracketed the $2.27 consensus and handset revenue is guided down mid-single digits; it targets data-centre revenue above $650 million in Q1. AppLovin jumped about 22% after hours on a beat, while Arm slipped 1.8% despite beating.
items.title: Qualcomm falls about 7% after hours as handset guidance weakens on Apple's ramp-down
items.whyItMatters: Weaker handset chip demand is another sign memory costs and Apple's modem switch are squeezing the phone supply chain.

items.confirm: Korean chip stocks keep falling through the session.
items.kill: A rebound as US megacap gains spill over.
items.source: TradingKey; Dimsum Daily; Peter's Asian Briefing
items.summary: Korea's Kospi traded about 2.7% lower near 5,529 early on Thursday, with SK hynix down 6.1%, Samsung 3.4% and SoftBank 6.2% in Tokyo, while the Nikkei opened 0.3% higher (TradingKey). Oracle cancelled a $7 billion deal to lease up to 100,000 AI chips to Tencent, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng opened about 400 points higher at 24,316 as Tencent rose about 3%.
items.title: Kospi falls about 2.7% as SK hynix drops 6% on fears Congress will scrutinise AI capex
items.whyItMatters: Asia's AI hardware names are giving back gains as US politics and Texas policy threaten data-centre spending.

items.confirm: Foreign buying continues for a third day.
items.kill: Foreign investors turn sellers after the gap-up.

seeds.why: Realty led with a 2.85% sector gain.

items.summary: Foreign investors bought a net ₹7,284 crore of Indian shares in the cash market on Wednesday (gross buys ₹21,607 crore) after ₹6,837 crore on Tuesday, while domestic institutions sold a net ₹3,712 crore (5paisa). Media (+5.15%), realty (+2.85%) and metal (+2.80%) led the sectors.
items.title: Foreign investors buy ₹7,284 crore of Indian shares, a second straight day above ₹6,800 crore
items.whyItMatters: Two days of near-record foreign buying are driving the Nifty's run and the rupee's recovery.

items.confirm: Execution guidance confirms the order value.
items.kill: Orders come in at the low end or margins disappoint.

nse.why: Wins up to ₹28,000 crore of orders.

items.summary: BHEL secured four orders from Adani Power for four 2×800 MW thermal projects, worth ₹20,000–28,000 crore, and its shares were up 5.5% at about ₹422 at noon on Wednesday; its order book is about ₹2.57 lakh crore (Kotak Neo).
items.title: BHEL wins four Adani Power thermal orders worth up to ₹28,000 crore
items.whyItMatters: Large thermal orders keep BHEL's revenue visibility high as India adds coal capacity for peak demand.

items.confirm: Brokerages raise estimates on margins.
items.kill: Investors focus on any slowdown in the pharmacy business.
items.summary: Apollo Hospitals reported consolidated profit of ₹630 crore (+32%) and revenue of ₹7,615 crore (+23%) after Wednesday's close, with EBITDA up 29% to ₹1,191 crore and a 15.64% margin (Upstox). The stock had closed at ₹8,599.50 (+1.89%) before the results.
items.title: Apollo Hospitals' profit rises 32% to ₹630 crore as revenue grows 23%
items.whyItMatters: Apollo's margins set the tone for listed hospital chains, a sector trading at premium valuations.

items.confirm: Volumes guidance points to a rebound.
items.kill: Investors sell on the sequential decline.

nse.why: Results: strong on the year, softer on the quarter.

items.summary: BSE reported consolidated profit of ₹809.15 crore (+44.9% year on year, −7.4% on the quarter) and revenue of ₹1,432.66 crore (+34.1%, −8.5% sequentially), and its board approved accepting an MMRDA offer for a plot at Bandra Kurla Complex, without terms. The stock fell 1.77% to ₹3,600.90 before the results.
items.title: BSE's profit rises 45% to ₹809 crore; board clears Bandra Kurla Complex plot proposal
items.whyItMatters: The sequential dip shows exchange earnings cooling after SEBI's derivatives curbs, even as annual growth stays strong.

items.confirm: The stock outperforms the pharma index.
items.kill: Investors discount one-offs in the US business.
items.summary: Aurobindo Pharma reported record revenue of ₹10,263 crore (+23.9%), profit of ₹1,124 crore (+32.5%) and EBITDA of ₹2,156 crore (+28.5%) on 4 Nov, and declared an interim dividend of ₹7 (TaxGuru).
items.title: Aurobindo Pharma posts record revenue of ₹10,263 crore and a 32.5% profit rise
items.whyItMatters: Aurobindo's growth stands out in a pharma results week where Lupin, Zydus and Biocon all reported lower profit.

items.confirm: Pharma index lags as brokers cut estimates.
items.kill: Investors look through margins to revenue growth.
items.summary: Lupin's profit fell 22.2% to ₹1,155 crore on revenue up 11.1% to ₹7,827 crore, with EBITDA margin down to 27.9% from 35.6% (Kotak Neo); Zydus Lifesciences' profit fell 27% to ₹926 crore on revenue up 29%, with margin down to 23.95% from 32.9%, and its shares were down 3.84% at 1 pm on Wednesday (Upstox). Biocon's profit fell 57.3% to ₹56.7 crore.
items.title: Lupin and Zydus profits fall 22–27% as US generic margins shrink
items.whyItMatters: Shrinking margins on high-value US generics are cutting pharma earnings even as revenue grows.

items.confirm: Utilities outperform on the results.
items.kill: Monsoon-driven hydro gains are seen as one-off.
items.summary: NHPC reported consolidated profit of ₹1,550 crore (+51.8%) on revenue of ₹4,482 crore (+33.2%) (SAHI), and Torrent Power reported revenue of ₹9,801 crore (+24%), EBITDA of ₹1,988 crore (+26%) and total comprehensive income of ₹835 crore (+14%) (Free Press Journal).
items.title: NHPC's profit jumps 52% to ₹1,550 crore; Torrent Power's revenue rises 24%
items.whyItMatters: Strong hydro and distribution earnings support the power utilities rally as demand rises.

items.confirm: Exide holds its gains as brokers upgrade.
items.kill: Lead prices rise and erase the margin gain.

nse.why: Margins up 2.7 points on price hikes.

items.summary: Exide Industries reported profit of ₹386 crore (+75.1%) on revenue of ₹5,026 crore (+20.3%), with EBITDA margin up to 12.1% from 9.4% on price hikes, and its shares rose as much as about 7% to ₹373 on Wednesday (Upstox).
items.title: Exide's profit jumps 75% to ₹386 crore as price hikes lift margins
items.whyItMatters: Battery makers are passing on costs, a sign of firm replacement and auto demand.

items.confirm: The stock re-rates on margins.
items.kill: Valuation (5.5x the sector P/E) caps any gain.
items.summary: Lenskart Solutions reported profit of ₹232.5 crore (+124.7%) on revenue of ₹2,845 crore (+35.7%) on 4 Nov (Inc42).
items.title: Lenskart's profit more than doubles to ₹233 crore as revenue rises 36%
items.whyItMatters: One of the newest consumer listings is showing operating leverage, which supports premium valuations for retail growth stocks.

items.confirm: Stock holds on the dividend.
items.kill: Investors sell on flat loan growth.
items.summary: Power Finance Corporation reported consolidated profit of ₹7,681.51 crore (−1.95%) on revenue of ₹29,044.48 crore (+0.5%), and declared a second interim dividend of ₹4.10 a share with a 17 Nov record date (Free Press Journal).
items.title: PFC's profit slips 2% to ₹7,682 crore; board declares ₹4.10 dividend
items.whyItMatters: Flat earnings at the biggest power lender show loan growth slowing even as power capex rises.

items.confirm: A 25 bp hike with a hawkish vote split.
items.kill: The BoE holds as oil falls.
items.summary: The Bank of England is expected to raise Bank Rate by 25 bp to 4.00% from 3.75% today, its first increase since August 2023, with a Reuters poll pointing to a 7–2 vote; UK inflation was 3.5% in September (Reuters via AOL).
items.title: Bank of England expected to raise rates to 4% today, its first hike since 2023
items.whyItMatters: A BoE hike would join the Fed's September hike in a global tightening turn driven by oil-led inflation.

mood: Risk-on: Democrats' sweep of Congress sent the Dow up 3%, Brent down 8.7% and gold up 3.4%, and GIFT Nifty points to a gap-up, but AI hardware stocks are sliding on data-centre worries.
